extracted.intended_audience: authors using ChemRxiv / chemistry researchers preparing preprints
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors submitting review-article preprints to ChemRxiv, including what types of review content are accepted and how to classify submissions. Focused on scope and content-type selection for preprint posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews must provide well-sourced context from multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.description: ChemRxiv will accept reviews that provide well-sourced context for previous research from multiple sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should synthesize and contextualize prior work across multiple sources rather than presenting unreferenced opinion or single-source summaries. This is part of ChemRxiv's expanded scope to include review preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded formats: short letters, commentaries, opinions, purely hypothetical works
rubrics_metrics.description: ChemRxiv will not accept short format letters/commentaries/opinions or purely hypothetical works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that are brief opinions, commentary pieces, short letters, or works that are purely speculative/hypothetical are out of scope and should not be submitted as 'review' preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate Content Type on submission: 'working paper' or 'review'
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission authors are asked to select a Content Type, choosing from 'working paper' (for any preprint containing new research results) or 'review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify your manuscript correctly: use 'working paper' for new research results and 'review' for review-article preprints that meet the review criteria above. For more details consult the submission FAQs or contact curator@chemrxiv.org.
